blocks.text: *Gear that shapes your skills, your defense, and your look.*
Weapons decide which skills you may use

Your weapon is more than a stat stick — its **type** decides which of the skills you have learned you may use right now (see *Skills*), and a weapon raises one of those skills through its **trademark** (below). Every weapon is a real 3D object your character holds.
The weapon roster

Every weapon owns a **distinct playstyle** — one clear reason to wield it. That playstyle isn't a design label: each of the fourteen is what the artist kept of one of the **Fourteen Kashira**, and how the weapon fights *is* how that Kashira fought (see **The World of Unwritten** and **The Whole Story**). **Mastery raises** lists the three stats that grow as your mastery of that weapon does — +0.5% each per mastery level. They fall into four families:
Might — physical power, up close

rows: Wide cleaves that hit every enemy in a broad arc; built to wipe out packs, not to duel.
Control enemies by denying their actions.
Stuns and knocks back, interrupting what enemies were about to do.
Pulls enemies in, dashes through their line, and cuts the defence of whatever it moves.
Overwhelm with physical bursts, or stand in front and take the hits — or both.

Two paths, chosen by the skills you learn. **Offence:** builds energy, then spends all your MP on one enormous physical blow; energy blasts that still deal physical damage. **Defence:** taunts, cuts damage taken, blocks, sends damage back. Build one path or mix both.

blocks.text: Finesse — precision & mobility

rows: Slows enemies and dashes away to keep its distance; fights on the move.
Kill slowly with poison from the blade.
Stacks poison on one target with every hit; the poison does its damage over time.
Nysara, the Face Without a Name
Finish targets with chains of critical hits.
Raises its crit chance and crit damage as the fight goes on; finishes low-health targets.

blocks.text: Arcane — magic

rows: Area nukes, Burn, and Freeze and slows to lock an area down.
Heals, regeneration, damage shields, buffs, and Cleanse.

blocks.text: Hybrid — two families in one

rows: Win duels through precise single-target bursts and timed defence.
Fast strike combos that burst one enemy down; parries and braces at the right moment to win the exchange.
Stacks Bleed; gains speed and a damage buff that keeps rising while it keeps attacking; gives up all defence to do it.
Many blades: thrown, they bounce through a crowd; swung, one swing lands two or three times.

**Thrown:** normal attacks, and some skills, bounce to nearby enemies. **Swung:** each swing can hit two or three times, and never bounces; its signature blow drops your HP to 1 for one huge physical hit.
melee or ranged — whichever of your STR or DEX is higher
Silence, defence cut and mana drain that wear an enemy down over a long fight.
Land one painful shot from as far away as possible.
One magic shot that can crit — the only magic in the game that can; the further the target, the more it hurts; the longest reach in the game.

blocks.text: Each weapon type has a deep pool of skills, but **a weapon carries none of them**. You learn a skill by spending that kind of weapon's mastery points on it, and it is yours for good — what you hold only decides which of the ones you know you may use right now. See *Skills* for how they are learned.
Equipment slots
Beyond your weapon, you wear:

items: **Body**, **Garment** and **Shoes** — each in **metal**, **leather** or **cloth**. On your **Head** you wear a hat, which is not armour: each of the fifteen hats adds a few stats and one effect, shown on its card, and the same on every copy. There is no off-hand: blocking and sending damage back come from the Fist's defence skills.

blocks.text: Every armour piece rolls **one word** as it drops, from its own slot's words, and wears it in its name — *+7 Tireless Iron Sabatons [C]*. A word does one thing, grows with the piece's grade, and never changes. No word appears on two slots, so you can never wear the same word twice. The Chainmail and Iron Sabatons you start in have none.

rows: Fewer critical hits land on you
Stuns, freezes, silences and ailments on you end sooner
Less damage from Fire · Water · Earth · Wind
Knockbacks and pulls move you a shorter distance

blocks.text: There is no ring slot: your **Ring** is part of you, not something you wear (see *Stats & the Ring*).

Each piece adds what it is worth — attack on a weapon; on armour, what its material buys — plus its word, plus any stats written onto it with **Ink** (see *Crafting & Recycling*). What it is worth starts from its **base**, and its **folds** and its **grade** build on that.
The base, and folds (+N)

**Every piece has a base.** A weapon's base follows how long its swing takes — and a heavier weapon swings slower — so every weapon deals the same damage a second at equal gear: a Common dagger's is **50** attack, a sword's **63**, a greatsword's **80** (a staff, wand or scythe gives magic attack instead). On armour, the **material** decides what the base buys — **metal** defence and HP, **leather** attack speed and evasion, **cloth** magic defence and MP — and shoes give half of what body armour or a garment give. A piece a monster drops rolls its base at **85% to 115%**; anything else — what you start in, what a shop sells, a reward — has the usual 100%. Hover a piece to see it: *Base 54 (108%)*.

The **+N** on a piece is how many times it has been **folded** at its station. Each fold costs **Temper Dust** — one at Raw, and one more for each grade — plus Unsigned, and adds a share of the base: **10%** a fold at Raw, rising to **70%** a fold at A. A quench that succeeds adds far more — **100%** of the base to reach F, up to **600%** to reach A — and everything a piece has climbed through stays on it. So a Common sword is **100** attack at Raw +10, **250** at F +10 and **2,500** at A +10.

**Every grade stops at +10**, and a piece is quenched only from there. From +4 a fold can fail and take one fold back. Nothing is wasted for good: half of what a piece's folds and quenches took comes back if you recycle it, and never less than 1 Temper Dust (see *Crafting & Recycling*).
Quality

Every piece carries a **quality grade**. A freshly dropped piece is **Raw**; above that the ladder runs **F, E, D, C, B, A**, and A is the best there is. Quality is decided by the **quench**: it lifts a piece one rung, to +0, or fails — never a jump. **A higher grade is always stronger**: an A +0 piece is worth more than eight times an F +10 one.

**Quality decides five things.** How much each **fold** adds and what the quench that reached it added; how big an armour piece's **word** is; how many **stats** can be written onto it with Ink; how far your **mastery** with it can go; and, on a weapon, how much its **trademark** raises its skill — **+5%** at Raw up to **+20%** at A.
Where a weapon's skills come from

**A weapon carries no skills.** You learn them yourself: fighting with that kind of weapon raises its mastery, every mastery level gives one point, and you spend points on its skills. Every skill names the **mastery level** at which it can be bought, and some name a skill that needs a point first. What you have learned is yours for good — the weapon in your hands only decides which of them you may use and how far its mastery can still grow. Every skill level you bought counts with any weapon of that kind.

**A weapon has a trademark.** As it drops it rolls one skill of its type and is named for it — a sword that empowers Thousand Petals is itself called **Thousand Petals**, and folded to +7 at grade C it reads **+7 Thousand Petals [C]** in your bag and on its card. The name never changes. Any skill of the weapon's pool that has a number to raise can come up: **1%** of weapons carry an ultimate's, the other **99%** an active's or a passive's, and inside each group every skill is equally likely — on a sword each of the fifteen actives and passives comes up **6.6%** of the time and each of the three ultimates **0.33%**. The Sword you start with has none. *Database ▸ Equipment* lists every trademark's chance. While you hold the weapon, **every** number that skill puts out is raised by **+5%** at Raw, rising with the grade to **+20%** at A — a Thousand Petals sword raises Thousand Petals' strike and its damage buff alike. Every trademark skill, on any weapon or none, is also **efficient** one cast in twenty, raising those numbers by a further +20% (see *Skills*). Right-click the weapon to see which skill and which numbers; right-click the skill to see the bonus on its own line.

**Gear has no rarity — what makes a piece better is its grade, its folds, its Ink and its card slots**, every one of them something you can work on. A piece's name ends with its card slots, **[1]** up to **[4]** on a weapon and up to **[2]** on armour; a piece with none shows nothing. Materials go by how hard they are to find, and their names and the squares behind them in your bag are coloured to match: **Temper Dust** and **Quench Oil** are Common (the ordinary text colour); **Watery Ink** and **Coarse Salt** Uncommon (green); **Thin Ink** and **Faint Ink** Rare (blue); **Clear Ink**, **Sharp Ink** and **Fine Salt** Epic (purple); **Pure Salt** Legendary (orange-gold).
So two people holding the same sword do not have the same skills: they have the skills they each chose.
Cards
Some gear has **card slots**. Cards are not in the game yet — see **Cards**.

text: *Status: the 14-weapon roster is locked, and every weapon can be held. The Katar, Shuriken, Wand, Scythe and Sniper borrow a dagger's, a staff's, an axe's or a bow's look until their own models arrive, the Fist fights bare-handed, every weapon swings with its own attack, and the Katar and the Axe are held one in each hand: each swing lands a second hit from the other hand at half power, with its own chance to miss and to crit. A Shuriken swings melee or ranged by your higher of STR or DEX, and thrown it bounces through up to 3 more enemies and comes back to your hand; a Sniper's normal attack is a magic shot that can crit and hits 2% harder for every metre to its target; the Shuriken's two-or-three-hit swings and the Fist's and Shuriken's all-in blows come with their skills, which are not in the game yet. Folding, quenching and the quality ladder are built; each weapon type's skill pool is being authored, and only the Sword's is finished today.*
